questions.question: The quadratic f(x) = (x − 3)² + 5 is in vertex form. What are the coordinates of the vertex?
questions.explain: Vertex form a(x−h)²+k places the vertex at (h, k), so here h = 3 and k = 5. The most common trap is flipping the sign of the x-value: (x−3) means h = +3, not −3.

questions.question: Solve for x: x² = 49
questions.explain: Taking the square root of both sides gives x = ±7; both the positive and negative roots must be included. Forgetting the ± is the single most common mistake with the square-root method.

questions.question: What is the axis of symmetry for the parabola y = 2(x + 1)² − 4?
questions.explain: In the form a(x−h)²+k, the axis of symmetry is x = h, so here h = −1. A frequent error is grabbing the constant term (−4) or flipping the sign of the x-value.

questions.question: For the equation 2x² − 5x + 1 = 0, what is the value of the discriminant (b² − 4ac)?
questions.explain: The discriminant is (−5)² − 4(2)(1) = 25 − 8 = 17. Students often add instead of subtract (getting 33) or forget to multiply 4·a·c together (getting 21).

questions.question: A student in Kelowna throws a ball straight up. Its height in metres after t seconds is h(t) = −5t² + 20t + 2. What is the maximum height the ball reaches?
questions.explain: The maximum occurs at t = −b/(2a) = 2, giving h(2) = −20 + 40 + 2 = 22 m. A common slip is dropping the constant term or flipping its sign, which yields 20 m or 18 m.

questions.question: Solve x² − 6x + 9 = 0 by factoring. What is the solution set?
questions.explain: x² − 6x + 9 factors as (x−3)², giving one repeated root x = 3. Treating it like a difference of squares (x² − 9) and writing x = ±3 is the classic trap.

questions.question: Solve x² + 3x − 10 = 0 using the quadratic formula. What are the roots?
questions.explain: Applying x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac))/(2a) gives (−3 ± √49)/2 = (−3 ± 7)/2, so x = 2 or x = −5. The most common error is applying the wrong sign to b, producing x = −2 or x = 5.

questions.question: A phone graphing app displays f(x) = x² − 4x − 5. What is the range of this function?
questions.explain: With a > 0 the parabola opens upward, so the range is y ≥ (vertex y-value). The vertex y is f(2) = 4−8−5 = −9. Reversing the inequality (y ≤ −9) or reading the vertex x as the y-value are the top mistakes.

questions.question: A student in Kelowna is building a parabolic arch for a school art project. The arch touches the ground at x = −3 m and x = 5 m, and its peak is 8 m above the ground. A friend asks: how high is the arch exactly 1 m to the right of the left base (i.e. at x = −2 m)?
questions.explain: With roots −3 and 5, write f(x) = a(x+3)(x−5); the vertex at x = 1 gives a = −1/2. Then f(−2) = −1/2·(1)·(−7) = 3.5 m. A frequent error is answering with the vertex height (8 m) or using the wrong x-value.

questions.question: A student rewrites y = 2x² − 12x + 7 by completing the square. What is the vertex of the resulting parabola?
questions.explain: Completing the square: 2(x²−6x+9) − 18 + 7 = 2(x−3)² − 11, so the vertex is (3, −11). The most common mistake is forgetting to add back the +7, which leaves the y-value stuck at −18.

questions.question: A BC student is analysing a jump-rope trick. The handle height (in cm) after t seconds is h(t) = −100t² + 400t + 50. The student claims the handle reaches exactly 150 cm at only one moment. Is the student correct?
options: Yes, it reaches 150 cm at t = 2 s only
Yes, it reaches 150 cm at t = 1 s only
No, it reaches 150 cm at two different times
questions.explain: Setting h = 150 gives t² − 4t + 1 = 0, whose discriminant is 16 − 4 = 12 > 0, so there are two distinct times. A parabola below its peak crosses any horizontal line twice; claiming one time ignores the second intersection.

questions.question: A student is given f(x) = 3x² − 12x + 2 and a classmate presents g(x) = 3(x − 2)² − 10. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between f and g?
options: They are the same function; g is simply f written in vertex form
g is f shifted 2 units to the right
g is f shifted 10 units down
g is a vertical stretch of f by a factor of 3
questions.explain: Completing the square on 3x² − 12x + 2 gives exactly 3(x−2)² − 10, so the two expressions are identical. A common misconception is to read the (x−2) and the −10 as separate transformations applied to f, when they are just the expanded form of the same quadratic.
